title: NASA Seeks US Industry Plans for Commercial Space Stations
text:
NASA is advancing American leadership in space by taking the next step toward a future where commercial space stations lead the way in low Earth orbit. On Friday, the agency released its final Request for Proposals inviting industry to submit plans for the next generation of commercial space stations.

“In alignment with the President’s National Space Policy, NASA is committed to maintaining a sustained American presence in low Earth orbit long after the International Space Station retires,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “We will continue to need a place to conduct research, develop technologies, train crews, and prepare for missions to the Moon and Mars. Commercial space stations may provide that capability while creating new opportunities for American industry and allowing NASA to concentrate more of our resources on the near-impossible missions ahead.”

Building on the agency’s Ignition event earlier this year, NASA regularly has engaged with private industry to shape the agency’s future direction in low Earth orbit. This included publishing two Requests for Information in March to gather industry’s perspective on low Earth orbit destinations and transportation. The agency also published a draft Request for Proposals in July, followed by an industry day and one-on-one meetings that allowed interested companies to review and comment on the planned acquisition approach.

“We’ve made it clear that NASA will never give up its presence in low Earth orbit,” said Isaacman. “Since Ignition, we have spent a lot of time listening to industry and working through what it will take to make this transition successful. The opportunity is significant, but the economics ultimately have to work. We want to see credible plans, strong technical execution, and companies prepared to invest in destinations that can serve NASA while developing additional customers and markets of their own.”

Proposals are due Tuesday, Dec. 8, with contract awards expected in spring 2027.

Under the solicitation, NASA outlines requirements for companies interested in designing, building, testing, certifying, and operating commercial low Earth orbit destinations capable of providing end-to-end destination and transportation services for human spaceflight use.

NASA intends to award firm-fixed-price, multi-award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts supporting development, certification, and services for continued low Earth orbit research and exploration. This will allow NASA to select two or more contractors through early development, followed by a competitive task order for final design, test, and evaluation, as well as certification and services from one or more contractors.

Learn more about NASA’s missions on the agency’s website:

https://www.nasa.gov

zhTitle: NASA 尋求美國產業對商業太空站的計畫
zh:
NASA 正在透過邁向由商業太空站主導低地球軌道的未來，推動美國在太空領域的領導地位。週五，該機構發布了最終的徵求提案（RFP），邀請業界提交下一代商業太空站的計劃。

「依照總統的國家太空政策，NASA 致力於在國際太空站退役後，持續維持美國在低地球軌道的存在，」NASA 行政長官 Jared Isaacman 表示。「我們將繼續需要一個地方進行研究、開發技術、培訓宇航員，以及為前往月球和火星的任務做準備。商業太空站可能提供這種能力，同時為美國產業創造新的機會，並讓 NASA 能將更多資源集中在未來幾乎不可能完成的任務上。」

在今年早些時候的 Ignition 活動基礎上，NASA 定期與私人產業交流，以塑造該機構在低地球軌道的未來方向。這包括在三月發布兩份資訊徵集（RFI），以收集業界對低地球軌道目的地及運輸的觀點。該機構還在七月發布了徵求提案草案（Draft RFP），隨後舉辦了業界日及一對一會議，讓有興趣的公司檢視並對計劃中的採購方式發表意見。

「我們已經明確表達了 NASA 永遠不會放棄低地球軌道的存在，」Isaacman 說。「自 Ignition 以來，我們花了大量時間傾聽業界意見，並分析實現這一轉型所需的條件。這是一個重大機會，但經濟效益最終仍必須可行。我們希望看到可信的計劃、強有力的技術執行，以及願意投資於可服務 NASA 並同時開發自身額外客戶和市場的目的地的公司。」

提案截止日期為 12 月 8 日星期二，合約預計於 2027 年春季頒發。

根據徵求文件，NASA 列出了有興趣設計、建造、測試、認證及運營商業低地球軌道目的地的公司的要求，這些目的地需能為載人航天提供端到端的目的地和運輸服務。

NASA 擬頒發固定價格、多獎項、不定期交付/不定量（Firm-Fixed-Price, Multi-Award, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity）合約，以支持持續的低地球軌道研究與探索的開發、認證及服務。這將允許 NASA 通過早期開發階段選擇兩家或更多承包商，隨後透過競爭性任務單選定承包商，完成最終設計、測試和評估，以及認證和服務。

https://www.nasa.gov
